beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string only from a runtime secret source (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable or Azure Key Vault) and never commit it to repo, logs or seed fixtures; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
When connecting from Node.js use the MongoDB driver with unified topology (useUnifiedTopology: true) and new URL parser (useNewUrlParser: true) and explicitly set tls/ssl options so TLS is enforced.
Enable TLS/SSL (tls=true or equivalent) and certificate validation for all client connections to the managed cluster; do not disable certificate validation in production.

Configure an appropriate connection pool (maxPoolSize) for the Node process (for example 20–100 depending on concurrency) and reuse the single MongoClient instance across the app instead of creating a client per request.
Enable and rely on driver retryable writes and implement an application-level exponential-backoff retry policy for idempotent operations; treat transient network and throttling errors as retryable.

Choose a sensible partition/shard key for the collection (e.g., ticker or ticker + date_bucket) to avoid single-hot partitions and to keep related queries within one partition whenever you need transactional or efficient small-scoped queries.
Provision throughput appropriately and enable autoscale or monitor RU consumption; set alerts for RU throttling (429) and increase RU or redesign queries before scaling to avoid repeated throttles.
Add a TTL (expireAfterSeconds) to articles that are ephemeral (e.g., tweets/headlines) so old documents are automatically removed (for example 30 days) rather than accumulating indefinitely.

Create explicit indexes for fields used in queries: index ticker, created_at, sentiment_score and any fields used in join/filter (e.g., watchlist_id); create a text index on headline/body if you search full-text.

Store vector embeddings in a dedicated field (e.g., embedding) with a fixed dimensionality and create a vector index (HNSW or DiskANN) configured for that field; tune index HNSW parameters (M, efConstruction) and search-time ef for desired recall/latency.
Normalize vectors if using cosine similarity (store L2-normalized vectors) and keep vector dimension consistent across all documents; reject or log mismatched-dimension inserts.
Use upserts with a unique external id or dedupe key (seeded article_id or hash) to make ingestion idempotent; create a unique index on that external id to prevent duplicate articles.

Keep document size small: avoid storing large binary blobs or unnecessarily large fields (store full article text in blob storage or object store if very large); perform projection on queries to avoid shipping embeddings unless needed.

Avoid cross-partition multi-document transactions; if you need transactional consistency, design data so that a transaction is scoped to a single partition key value because distributed transactions are expensive or unsupported.
Handle 429/RequestRateTooLarge by reading and honoring Retry-After headers and implement exponential backoff with jitter; log 429s and create monitoring alerts when they spike.
Use explain() to validate queries are using the intended indexes; optimize queries to use indexed predicates and projections and avoid full-collection scans in production.

Protect secrets and rotate keys in production: prefer Azure Managed Identity or Azure Key Vault for long-term deployments rather than embedding connection strings or primary keys in environment variables.
Enable and collect driver and server metrics and diagnostics (latency, connection pool usage, RU consumption, 429s) and create alerts for throttling, high latency, or connection churn.

Protect the Express endpoint: require authentication/authorization for triggering scrapes or runs, rate-limit requests, validate inputs, and never expose direct DB admin endpoints or connection details.

For alerting against a watchlist, create a compound index tailored to the typical lookup (e.g., {ticker:1, active:1}) so the alert agent can efficiently find matches rather than scanning the watchlist collection.

Use explainable, reproducible seed and verification scripts that are idempotent (create-if-not-exists) and scoped to the sample_fintech_11 database; do not enumerate or modify other databases on the cluster.

When performing similarity search, limit result set and perform a cheap filtering pass (e.g., by ticker or created_at range) before nearest-neighbor search to reduce vector-search cost and RU consumption.

Encrypt sensitive fields at rest and in transit; rely on server-side encryption provided by the managed service, and consider client-side field-level encryption for PII or secrets stored in documents.

Monitor and guard against slow inserts/large bulk ingests: use bulkWrite with reasonable batch sizes and backoff on failures instead of one-by-one inserts under high throughput to avoid saturating RU/s.

Use change streams or a push-based mechanism (if available) to trigger downstream alerting instead of frequent polling; if change streams are unsupported, poll with a cursor on created_at and use last-seen watermark to minimize reads.
